errors.description: The two front panels are folded back against the sides rather than splayed fully flat out to the left and right as in the blueprint's completely opened-out layout.
errors.expected: Fully flat layout with both fronts splayed outward as wings.
errors.actual: Waistcoat opened and laid flat with the fronts turned back along the sides; the full interior lining zone is still exposed.
errors.correction: Acceptable - this is how a real waistcoat lies when opened, and the entire lining zone the blueprint shades is visible and unobstructed.

lockedFeatures: Interior/lining view, waistcoat opened and laid flat - CORRECT
Garment identity is a sleeveless waistcoat, not a jacket - CORRECT
PRINTED PLACEMENT ARTWORK on the lining cloth, bold and unmistakable at a glance - CORRECT (this was ABSENT on attempt 1 and is the defining feature of the option)
Lustrous silk/cupro lining with visible sheen - CORRECT
Lining coverage runs from neckline to the full shaped lower edge, entirely inside the frame - CORRECT (was cropped on attempt 1)
Armhole curves, shoulder line and neckline shape matching the blueprint layout - CORRECT
Centre-back seam running the full height - CORRECT
Vertical panel seam lines flanking the centre back in the drawn count and spacing - CORRECT
Dark navy cloth facings framing the lining zone at the outer edges, matching the blueprint's unshaded border - CORRECT
Left/right symmetry of the layout - CORRECT
Zero annotation: no numbers, arrows, leader lines, red guide marks or text - CORRECT
notes: Attempt 2 fixes the critical failure from attempt 1. The lining now carries a large decorative printed placement artwork centred on the back panel and continuing in scale across the adjoining panels, so the option is identifiable in under a second and cannot be confused with a plain-lining sibling. All the geometry that was already correct on attempt 1 - armholes, shoulder line, centre-back seam, panel seams, navy facings, symmetry - is preserved unchanged, and the previously cropped lower hem is now fully in frame.
